claim_verdicts.evidence: Lines 16-22: `Widget build(BuildContext context) { final apiClient = ApiClient(); return MaterialApp(title: 'Đơn Hàng', theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo, useMaterial3: true), home: ProductListScreen(apiClient: apiClient),);` inside `class DonHangApp extends StatelessWidget`. Code block 1 matches lines 15-23 verbatim.

Line 8: `class ProductListScreen extends StatefulWidget`; its only method is `createState()` (line 14). The `build` returning `Scaffold(appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Đơn Hàng'), actions: [IconButton(icon: const Icon(Icons.login) ...)]), body: FutureBuilder<List<Product>>(...), floatingActionButton: FloatingActionButton(...child: const Icon(Icons.refresh)))` is in `class _ProductListScreenState` (lines 17, 30-69). Rest (spinner on waiting, ListView.builder of ListTile with Text title/trailing) matches lines 46-65.

layout/index.md: "In Flutter, almost everything is a widget—even layout models are widgets. The images, icons, and text that you see in a Flutter app are all widgets. But things you don't see are also widgets, such as the rows, columns, and grids that arrange, constrain, and align the visible widgets." architectural-overview.md: "Widgets form a hierarchy based on composition. Each widget nests inside its parent"; "There are widgets for padding, alignment, rows, columns, and grids."

ui/index.md: "When a widget's state changes, the widget rebuilds its description, which the framework diffs against the previous description in order to determine the minimal changes needed in the underlying render tree to transition from one state to the next." declarative.md: widgets "are immutable and are only lightweight blueprints". Verified as written in the ledger; the lesson's stronger wording ('redraws only what differs') is NOT covered, see issue in 'How it works'.

android-devs.md: "Flutter's widgets are lightweight, in part due to their immutability." ui/index.md: "Although the parent creates a new instance of `ShoppingListItem` when it rebuilds, that operation is cheap because the framework compares the newly built widgets with the previously built widgets and applies only the differences". faq.md: "The Flutter framework uses a functional-style flow that depends heavily on the underlying memory allocator efficiently handling small, short-lived allocations."

Analogy limited to containment. Supported by: "Widgets form a hierarchy based on composition. Each widget nests inside its parent and can receive context from the parent. This structure carries all the way up to the root widget ... typically `MaterialApp` or `CupertinoApp`". HTML side is taught in the prereq frontend.l1.the-dom.

issues.quote: That screen's own `build` returns a `Scaffold`
issues.text: `ProductListScreen` has no `build` method: it `extends StatefulWidget` (line 8) and only defines `createState()`. The `build` returning the `Scaffold` is in `_ProductListScreenState` (lines 17, 30). Same error in the Try it suggested answer ("The `Scaffold` returned by `ProductListScreen`'s `build`"). A learner opening the file will not find `build` inside `class ProductListScreen`.
issues.fix: Replace both phrases with "the `build` method in `product_list_screen.dart`" and add once, in 'In the Đơn Hàng system': "(in this file `build` sits in the class `_ProductListScreenState` right below `ProductListScreen`; why is a later lesson)". Use claim 2's suggested_text for the ledger.

issues.quote: updates the screen only where they differ. ... Redrawing is done only for what actually changed.
issues.text: Unlisted claim: the lesson moves from the documented statement (framework diffs descriptions to find "the minimal changes needed in the underlying render tree"; "applies only the differences to the underlying RenderObject") to a paint-level claim that only changed parts are redrawn. The docs opened (ui/index.md, declarative.md, architectural-overview.md) do not say that. Repeated in misconception 2 ("only the changed part is drawn again", "stays smooth") and summary line 5 ("redraws only what differs").
issues.fix: Replace with: "Flutter compares that description with the previous one and changes only what differs; parts that did not change are kept, not rebuilt from scratch." Misconception 2: "...Flutter compares the new description with the previous one and applies only the differences." Drop "stays smooth". Summary 5: "Flutter compares the new description with the old and applies only the differences."

issues.quote: a round refresh button in the corner
issues.text: Unlisted claim, and wrong for this app: main.dart sets `useMaterial3: true`; in Flutter 3.47.2 SDK source (packages/flutter/lib/src/material/floating_action_button.dart:817, `_FABDefaultsM3`) a regular FAB's shape is `RoundedRectangleBorder(borderRadius: BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(16.0)))`, a rounded square, not a circle. Also in Try it: "3. The round button in the bottom corner."
issues.fix: Say "a refresh button in the bottom-right corner" in 'The situation' and "3. The refresh button in the bottom corner." in Try it. Do not describe its shape.

issues.quote: a `MaterialApp`, which sets the app's title and colours
issues.text: Next to 'The situation' ("a title bar reading 'Đơn Hàng'") this reads as if `MaterialApp.title` produces the title bar. SDK doc for WidgetsApp.title (3.47.2, widgets/app.dart:841): "A one-line description used by the device to identify the app for the user." The visible title bar text is the `AppBar`'s `Text`.
issues.fix: "...which sets the app's name shown by the browser tab and its colours..." (or drop "title" and keep "colours").

issues.quote: The Đơn Hàng app's tree runs `MaterialApp` → `ProductListScreen` → `Scaffold` → `FutureBuilder` → `ListView` → `ListTile` → `Text`.
issues.text: Presented as the tree, but it is only the widgets written in this app's code; `MaterialApp`, `Scaffold` and `ListView.builder` build further widgets of their own between these levels. Same for the 'How it works' diagram. Docs say "almost everything is a widget" (ui/layout/index.md); the lesson says "everything you see is a widget".
issues.fix: Summary 3: "In the Đơn Hàng code, the path runs `MaterialApp` → ... → `Text`." Add under the diagram: "Widgets written in the app's code; Flutter's own widgets add more levels in between."

issues.quote: False, because the tree is a cheap description that Flutter compares, redrawing only what differs.
issues.text: Key c is correct given the lesson, but option c and the explanations (correct: "redraws only what changed"; d: "Flutter does redraw, but only the parts that changed") carry the same overstated paint-level claim as the major 'How it works' issue.
issues.fix: Option c: "False, because the tree is a cheap description that Flutter compares, applying only the differences." Explanation correct: "...compares it with the previous one and applies only what changed." d: "Flutter does update the screen after the first frame, applying only the differences." Mirror in vi.
